requireStagingSibling_verbatim.moduleDoc: requireStagingSibling (CTX card B item 4): the county comes from the production run's flags, never from its own publish_runs row (which is inserted only after the bakes). The most recent succeeded staging publish for that county must carry a walk_id whose walk verdict is `pass` and whose sweep count is at least MIN_SWEEP_PARCELS. Each refusal has its own code so a vacuous pass (an unwalked sibling) and an always-refuse (no sibling ever found) are both impossible. (src/lib/publish-guards.mjs:1-15)
requireStagingSibling_verbatim.sql: SELECT pr.id, pr.status, pr.walk_id, pr.completed_at, sw.id AS walk_row_id, sw.body AS walk_body FROM publish_runs pr LEFT JOIN verify_walks sw ON sw.id = pr.walk_id WHERE pr.county_fips = $1 AND pr.target = 'staging' AND pr.status = 'succeeded' ORDER BY pr.completed_at DESC NULLS LAST, pr.created_at DESC LIMIT 1 (STAGING_SIBLING_SQL, src/lib/publish-guards.mjs:88-97)
requireStagingSibling_verbatim.constants: MAX_SIBLING_AGE_HOURS = 48 (publish-guards.mjs:33, with the note that the job's task timeout is 6h); MIN_SWEEP_PARCELS = 10 (publish-guards.mjs:40, 'A-021: gold plus an area-swept set; fewer than ten swept parcels is not a sweep'); refusal codes STAGING_SIBLING_REQUIRED, STAGING_SIBLING_UNWALKED, STAGING_SIBLING_FAILED, STAGING_SIBLING_NO_SWEEP, STAGING_SIBLING_STALE.
checksInOrder_verbatim: if (!row) refuse(STAGING_SIBLING_REQUIRED, "no succeeded staging publish for county");
const ageHours = (now.getTime() - completedAtMs) / (1000 * 60 * 60); if (!Number.isFinite(completedAtMs) || ageHours > maxAgeHours) refuse(STAGING_SIBLING_STALE, ...)
if (!row.walk_id || !row.walk_row_id || !body || typeof body !== "object") refuse(STAGING_SIBLING_UNWALKED, "staging sibling has no walk (walk_id null or walk row missing)", { siblingId: row.id });
if (body.publishRunId && body.publishRunId !== row.id) refuse(STAGING_SIBLING_UNWALKED, "linked walk names a different publish run", ...)
const count = Number(body.sweep?.count); if (!Number.isInteger(count) || count < minSweep) refuse(STAGING_SIBLING_NO_SWEEP, ...)
return { siblingId: row.id, walkId: row.walk_id, sweepCount: count };

reasoning.doesTheReMintDependOnThePublishCompletin: No measured dependency, and on the evidence they are independent stores: step 1 writes the Smart Site tier1 facet store for 48209 (re-measured below in this artifact: production already holds node:48209:84629 under run b5e54917), while step 2 writes the atom store that the record path spreads display_meta from. The panel's documented read order (CP1/A-128: the Property Explorer reads the atom chain and merges cortex only when the chain is empty) also means the conflict row's appearance does NOT wait on a fresh tier1 bake. So the re-mint does not need step 1 to have completed first.
reasoning.doesThePublishRiskOverwritingAReMintedAt: Not in the atom store (the publish job writes place_layer_snapshots, not the atoms table). The RISK is the reverse direction and it is real: the publish's inline sweep walk reads the SERVED surface, and the planner's own CTX-F item 1 note is that a staging bake on incomplete data poisons its own sibling walk and can then satisfy Rule 6 for a production publish on the same incomplete data (bastrop-publish.mjs:395-397). That is about data completeness, not atoms. The concrete unknown is whether the record snapshot refresh rewrites rows the publish just wrote. UNMEASURED -- name the store before interleaving anything.

contradictionsAndGaps.claim: Planner context: 'Production still 404s on 48209:84629, so step 4 is a real write.'
contradictionsAndGaps.measurement: BOTH HALVES ARE TRUE BUT THE INFERENCE IS NOT. Read-only GET of https://smartsite.cloud/api/spine/cortex/api/brokerage/v1/place/node/48209:84629/facets returns HTTP 404 in 0.94s -- the SERVED surface does 404. But SELECT against the production Neon store (PRODUCTION_NEONDB_URL) shows the ROW EXISTS: place_layer_snapshots, adapter_key='node-facets:tier1', place_key='node:48209:84629' returns 1 row with payload_json->>'publishRunId' = b5e54917-4f5a-461c-ad75-37b60016ca7d (the 2026-09-13 production run), has_baseFacts = true, has_recordRetirement = true, recordRetirement.status = 'retired', access {entitlement: anyone-free, discoverability: catalog-listed}.
contradictionsAndGaps.whyItMatters: A full, catalog-listed tier1 row for the exact parcel is sitting in the production store and the surface still 404s. So whatever step 4 fixes, it is NOT 'the store is empty' -- the 404 is produced by the serving/freshness layer, or by the read path, or by the row's own versioning, not by absence of data. Anyone who fires step 4 expecting to fill an empty store is reasoning from a wrong model, and any post-publish check that treats a 200 as proof the publish worked needs to explain why the pre-existing identical row served 404. One hypothesis I could NOT test: the freshness stamp for production:48209 may name a different run than the one stamped on the row. I looked for the stamp table in the Neon public schema (information_schema.tables where table_name like '%fresh%|%stamp%|%publish%') and found NOTHING -- so the freshness store is elsewhere (most likely the factory store), and reading it was blocked (see H2).
